items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: Jimmy was a good piano player, I mean a good trombone player. And Elmer Chambers, incidentally, was in the war with me. And Charley Dixon played very well... we had seven entertainers and there was five of us in the band.

ctx.x: At one little affair -- they were all having a great affair, and James P. Johnson came down there with his wife. And he was -- and his wife was a dancer, I don't recall what her name was then, her professional name was Lily Wright. And so she asked Jimmy to play for her, a piece, and she danced. And after she finished, she said, "Jimmy, would you like to play a piece?" Well, Jimmy played a piece. And that broke up the matinee. Because nobody wanted to go near that piano after Jimmy got through playing. The piano…

Lucky Roberts and James P. Johnson. Oh, they were the greatest for playing, now, for handling a song -- Eubie Blake could play a song behind a singer more legitimately. Along the lines of, but naturally (banging out a rag) for just nicely, (unintelligible), [there] was no comparison, because Art Tatum wasn't on the scene then.
